title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the 'equation des lacets', Grothendieck's own system of GT-type equations, studied in the extended profinite fundamental group \widetilde{\pi_{0,3}}^\wedge. This group carries the order-3 symmetry rho, which cyclically permutes 0, 1, infinity, and the involution sigma_infinity. The case h=1 is described by data alpha_0 in \widetilde{\pi_{0,3}}^\wedge, f in \pi_{0,3}^\wedge and nu in \hat Z, subject to
- (42) xi := alpha_0 rho(alpha_0) = l_0^nu phi, with phi := f sigma_infinity(f)^{-1};
- the cyclic relation xi rho(xi) rho^2(xi) = 1.
From these one sets g := sigma_infinity(f)^{-1} l_1^nu rho(f) = (l_0^nu f)^{-1} (l_0^nu phi) rho(l_0^nu f).

On this page Grothendieck tests the relations in a linear quotient. pi_{0,3} is realised as the Sanov subgroup of SL(2,Z) generated by l_0 = [[1,-2],[0,1]] = epsilon_0^2 and l_1, and the extended group maps to \widetilde{SL}(2,\hat Z). Lifting alpha_0 and f there is ambiguous up to sign. Pushing everything down to SL(2,\hat Z) gives the following.
1. xi and phi are well defined independently of the sign choices. Hence (44) xi = epsilon l_0^nu phi holds in SL(2,\hat Z) for a well-determined epsilon in {+-1}. The question is whether epsilon = +1.
2. rho(l_0) = l_1 holds in SL(2,\hat Z) with no sign correction. So the second expression for g is valid there, and g is a rho-twisted conjugate of l_0^nu phi.
3. One has g rho(g) rho^2(g) = epsilon_0 * 1 with epsilon_0 = +-1.
4. The 'norm' N(g) = g rho(g) rho^2(g) transforms under twisted conjugation g' = a g rho(a)^{-1} as N(g') = a N(g) rho^3(a)^{-1}. The element implementing rho has cube -1, which is central, so rho^3 = id as an automorphism. Hence N(g') = epsilon_0 * 1 as well.
5. Apply this to g' = l_0^nu phi = epsilon xi: N(epsilon xi) = epsilon^3 N(xi) = epsilon, since N(xi) = 1 is inherited from the profinite group. Therefore epsilon_0 = epsilon.

Conclusion, stated on the next page: the validity of xi = l_0^nu phi in SL(2,\hat Z) is equivalent to g rho(g) rho^2(g) = 1, which is left open. The page thus serves as a consistency and sign check of the loop equations after projection to the congruence (SL_2) quotient.
errors: Notational inconsistency with the next page: here xi = alpha_0 rho(alpha_0), but on the next page xi is defined as alpha_0 rho(alpha_0)^{-1} (in GL(2,\hat Z), with det alpha_0 = +-1).

The remark 'rho^3 = -1' is loose. rho is an automorphism, and as an automorphism rho^3 = id. What has cube -1 is the element of SL(2,Z) implementing rho. The argument only needs rho^3(a) = a, which holds because -1 is central, so the reasoning is correct.

In (44) the factor is written 'sigma_0 f^{-1}', which should be sigma_infinity(f)^{-1}, consistent with (42)/(43). The page uses l_0^nu in (44) but l_1^nu in g on the previous page; these are reconciled by rho(l_0) = l_1.

ideas.what: Testing the GT/loop equations in the image of the extended profinite pi_{0,3} in (\widetilde)SL(2,\hat Z), tracking the central sign ambiguity
ideas.modern_name: GT action on the congruence/SL_2 quotient of \hat F_2 (Sanov subgroup Gamma(2)); central extension \hat B_3 -> \widetilde{SL}(2,\hat Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (GT, 1990); Ihara; Lochak–Schneps and Nakamura on GT and SL_2/mapping-class-group quotients
ideas.where_published: Not in the Esquisse; La Longue Marche discusses the Teichmüller tower but not this computation as far as I know (unsure)

ideas.what: Norm map N(g) = g rho(g) rho^2(g) for an order-3 automorphism, invariant up to conjugation under twisted conjugation g -> a g rho(a)^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: Nonabelian cohomology H^1(Z/3, G) / twisted conjugacy; norm of a cocycle

ideas.what: Reduction of the sign question epsilon = +1 in xi = epsilon l_0^nu phi to the cyclic relation g rho(g) rho^2(g) = 1
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of hexagon-type (3-cycle) relation under projection to SL_2

missed.claim: Grothendieck leaves open whether the sign epsilon equals +1, equivalently whether g rho(g) rho^2(g) = 1, in SL(2,\hat Z) for solutions of the loop equation (case h=1). This is a small concrete question about the SL_2-image of GT-type data, likely decidable by direct computation.
missed.quote: avec un signe ε∈{±1} bien déterminé, et la question qui se pose est si on a ε=+1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It bears on whether Grothendieck's loop equations descend sign-free to the congruence quotient, a detail relevant when comparing his system with Drinfeld's GT relations. It is probably settled implicitly by known results on GT acting on SL_2 quotients.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine sign-bookkeeping computation within Grothendieck's unpublished loop-equation programme. The open sign question is minor and of limited significance given later GT literature.
transcription_corrections: In (44), 'f σ_0 f^{-1}' should read f σ_∞(f)^{-1}.
Line 3 likely reads 'des choix de signes, [de α_0 et de f], et de même g' rather than 'et de = g' (uncertain).

The NB reads roughly '(NB on n'a pas ρ^3=1 dans Sl(2,Ẑ), mais ρ^3=-1, ce qui n'implique pas que l'automorphisme ... ρ est d'ordre 3 ...), d'où ε_0 = ε'; the final conclusion 'ε_0 = ε' is clearly written.
